Exclusive: Samsung is working on a private cloud for Galaxy AI, and it could look a lot like Apple’s

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals an unreleased "SPAC" framework to process anonymized cloud-based Galaxy AI requests.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 10:06 AM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 points to “SPAC,” a new Samsung framework for processing AI requests on its servers while keeping them private.

• SPAC appears to closely follow Apple’s Private Cloud Compute blueprint, and the code references AI models like Google’s Gemma 4 and Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6.

• SPAC doesn’t seem to be active on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet, and Samsung hasn’t announced it either.

Galaxy AI has always made you choose between privacy and capability. Features that run on your phone keep your data there. However, the more capable ones, like Writing assist, Note assist, and generative photo edits, send your data to Samsung’s servers. Samsung’s current promise for those is a policy one: Photo Editor, for instance, tells you your image “will be sent to servers for processing… but not stored by Samsung.” If you’d rather not take that on trust and face value, the only option is the “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings, which switches those cloud-based features off entirely.

Apple pitched a way around that trade-off two years ago when it launched Private Cloud Compute with Apple Intelligence in iOS 18. Private Cloud Compute (PCC) promises to extend device-level privacy to server-side AI processing: your request still goes to a server, but it’s encrypted, anonymized, and processed in a way that even Apple says it can’t access. Google and Meta have since built their own versions, with Google promising your personal data stays private to you and is not accessible to anyone else, “not even Google.” Now, code in the One UI 9.5 beta suggests Samsung is building its own take on the idea, and it looks a lot like Apple’s.

Samsung’s “SPAC” and “Arcane” are new in One UI 9.5

Digging through One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on our Galaxy S26 Ultra over the past week, we found a new Samsung SDK called “SPAC” inside four apps: Photo Editor, IntelliVoiceService (Samsung’s speech and language service), Smart Capture, and PhotoRemasterService. None of these apps had it in One UI 9.

Based on the code, SPAC seemingly connects to a server-side gateway that Samsung’s code calls “Arcane”, alongside separate token, identity, and fraud detection services.

While we looked around, we could not find what SPAC stands for. If we’re allowed to guess, it could refer to “Samsung Private AI Cloud,” but it could just as easily be called something else. (Yes, SPAC also stands for Special Purpose Acquisition Company, the shell companies used to take businesses public. We don’t know whether this is coincidental or intentional — probably the former rather than the latter.)

SPAC appears to be designed so your AI requests stay private

It’s early days, but it seems most of SPAC’s code deals with privacy and trust rather than AI. Based on the code, it appears to work in a few layers:

• A middleman for your requests: User requests appear to pass through a third-party relay first, so Samsung can see what you asked but not where it came from.

• Servers that have to prove themselves: Your phone appears to check that Samsung’s server is running genuine, untampered software before it sends anything.

• A public-style record: Samsung’s server software appears to be logged in a record that can’t be quietly changed, so it can’t swap in something different for some users.

• Anonymous passes: Your phone appears to get one-time passes that prove you’re a real Galaxy user without revealing which user you are.

The code also includes an “unattested” mode in which the phone skips some of these checks, but this could be for internal testing only.

SPAC seems to follow the blueprint Apple laid out for Private Cloud Compute

Apple

Apple explained how Private Cloud Compute works back in June 2024, and Samsung’s SPAC looks remarkably similar so far.

In Apple’s system, requests carry no identifying information. They’re approved with one-time passes that aren’t tied to you, and they go through a third-party relay that hides your IP address. Apple also logs its server software in a public record that can’t be quietly changed, and iPhones only send data to servers that match that record. SPAC’s code appears to have a match for almost every one of those pieces.

Apple

Apple isn’t the only one doing this. Google’s Private AI Compute, which launched in November 2025, also sends requests through third-party relays to hide where they came from, and uses anonymous passes to keep your identity separate from your AI requests. Meta’s Private Processing for WhatsApp’s AI features works much the same way, with outside companies running the relay and the public record.

So far, it doesn’t seem like Samsung is inventing anything new here. It appears to be adopting what has become the industry’s standard recipe for private cloud AI, spelled out first by Apple. If anything, Samsung is late to the party. Apple, Google, and Meta all announced their systems publicly and explained how they work. Samsung hasn’t said a word yet about its plans for a private cloud AI system for users, but SPAC might just be it.

SPAC’s code references Gemma 4, Qwen 3.6, and FLUX.2

SPAC code within the above-mentioned apps references open-weight AI models from Google and Alibaba, which Samsung could run on its own servers. We couldn’t confirm that Galaxy AI uses any of them right now on our Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

The above code snippet is from Smart Capture, which powers the AI select feature, and it shows the app relying on Alibaba’s Qwen 3.6 and Google’s Gemma 4 as options. IntelliVoiceService references Gemma 4, while PhotoRemasterService references Black Forest Labs’ FLUX.2 klein 4B and a Stable Diffusion model.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Photo Editor also makes reference to OpenAI’s TTS models, Samsung’s own Gauss, and Meta’s V-JEPA, but doesn’t seem to be using them.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Which Galaxy AI features could use SPAC?

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Based on the code, several Galaxy AI features could use SPAC. AI select could get smarter at understanding what’s on your screen, for instance, pulling several events from a screenshot into your calendar at once. Photo Editor’s cloud AI eraser and cloud photo upscaling, including zoomed camera shots, appear set to move to SPAC. So does live speech translation, through a route Samsung’s own code labels “private.”

The code also maps everyday Galaxy AI tasks like summarizing, tone changes, emoji suggestions, writing help, and Now Brief to SPAC, along with an unnamed “GUI agent” and something called “Bixby work.” If all of this moves over, a large part of Galaxy AI’s cloud features could eventually run through SPAC instead of Samsung’s current servers.

SPAC doesn’t seem to be live on the Galaxy S26 Ultra yet

On our S26 Ultra, SPAC appears to be switched off for now:

• Smart Capture and Photo Editor only use SPAC on a newer Galaxy AI version than our S26 Ultra reports, the same gate as Recompose.

• PhotoRemasterService needs a newer Remaster version than the S26 Ultra has.

• IntelliVoiceService only uses SPAC for translation when an app asks for a “private” cloud mode, and we could not trigger this yet.

We used Writing assist, AI select, Note assist, Now Brief, and Interpreter while logging the phone’s activity. None of them touched SPAC, and all of them used Samsung’s existing Galaxy AI cloud or ran on the device. There’s also no user-facing text about SPAC anywhere in the build, so there’s no new consent screen or privacy notice yet. So while code about SPAC does exist in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra, it doesn’t seem to work right now.

It’s also not yet clear how SPAC will work with the existing “Process data only on device” toggle in Galaxy AI Settings. We found Photo Editor checking the toggle, but not Smart Capture’s or IntelliVoiceService’s SPAC code, though Samsung could be handling it elsewhere in One UI.

Samsung’s servers, on the other hand, appear to be further along than the phone software. Public certificate records show production server addresses for SPAC that Samsung has kept renewing over the past few months, and newer entries suggest it’s adding servers in the US as well.

The back end for SPAC could already be in place, waiting for the features to switch on.

A private cloud could matter for Galaxy AI

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

If SPAC works as the early code in this beta suggests, Samsung could swap today’s “not stored by Samsung” policy promise for one it can prove: running more powerful Galaxy AI features in the cloud while keeping your requests about as private as on-device processing.

Such a change would put Galaxy AI on equal footing with Apple Intelligence and Gemini on privacy. It could also matter more if Samsung starts charging for Galaxy AI Premium and leans harder on server-side models.

We’ve reached out to Samsung for more details on SPAC, and we’ll update this article when we hear back.

items.title: LG’s S6FTR 5.1 soundbar with rear speakers is $180 off
items.summary: LG's 5.1-channel soundbar kit with a subwoofer and wireless rear speakers is 45% off, its lowest price yet.
items.body:

Audio

LG's S6FTR 5.1 soundbar with rear speakers is $180 off

LG's 5.1-channel soundbar kit with a subwoofer and wireless rear speakers is 45% off, its lowest price yet.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 9:49 AM ET

•

•

Amazon

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

LG’s S6FTR soundbar kit just dropped to its lowest price. The complete 5.1-channel system is down to $219.99 on Amazon, which is $180 off its $399.99 list price and $30 below its previous low of $249.99.

The LG S6FTR comes with everything you need for surround sound in one box. Alongside the main soundbar, there’s a subwoofer for deeper bass and a pair of rear speakers to place behind your seating. With Dolby Audio support, effects in movies and games can move around the room instead of coming only from the front.

The rear speakers connect to the soundbar wirelessly, with no extra receiver needed. They are linked to each other with a cable, and one of them plugs into the wall, so it’s worth planning your layout around a nearby outlet.

Owners of compatible LG TVs get an extra perk. WOW Orchestra lets the TV’s speakers and the soundbar work together for a fuller sound, and it’s a neat way to get more out of hardware you already have.

The setup is a good fit for living rooms where a TV’s built-in speakers struggle with dialogue and bass, and it’s much simpler than piecing together a receiver and separate speakers.

At $219.99, the LG S6FTR is one of the more affordable ways to get true 5.1 surround sound with real rear speakers this holiday season.

items.title: Amazon’s Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is $150 off for Black Friday
items.summary: Amazon's 12-inch Android tablet with Google Play drops to a record-low $349.99, $50 below last week's deal price.
items.body:

Mobile

Amazon's Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is $150 off for Black Friday

Amazon's 12-inch Android tablet with Google Play drops to a record-low $349.99, $50 below last week's deal price.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 9:18 AM ET

•

•

Amazon

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

A big tablet for streaming, reading, and browsing from the couch makes a lot of sense this time of year, and Amazon’s largest new model just got its best discount. The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is down to $349.99 on Amazon, which is $150 off its $499.99 list price and a new record low. It was $399.99 last week.

The biggest change from Amazon’s older Fire tablets is the software. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs Android with the Google Play Store built in, so the apps you already use on your phone, from Netflix and YouTube to Google Docs, are a quick download away. Alexa is still on board for hands-free help around the house.

The 12-inch 2.8K display is the star for entertainment. It’s roomy enough for movies and TV shows, comfortable for comics and e-books, and big enough to run two apps side by side when you want to keep a recipe open while checking messages.

Amazon pairs that screen with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, which leaves plenty of space to download shows for a long weekend away from Wi-Fi. Amazon also promises all-day battery life, so it can handle a full day of on-and-off use without hunting for a charger.

At $349.99, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is a far easier buy than it was at launch, whether it’s for the whole family or a gift for someone who wants a big Android tablet with Alexa built in.

Audio

Save $230 on Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones in Midnight Blue

Sony's noise canceling headphones are 57% off in Midnight Blue, $28 under the $198 deals they've hit all year.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 9:10 AM ET

•

•

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

Sony’s WH-1000XM5 have dropped to $198 several times this year, but today’s deal goes further. The Midnight Blue pair is down to $169.99 on Amazon, which is $230 off the $399.99 list price and $28 below those earlier deals. Black and Silver aren’t currently sold by Amazon, so Midnight Blue is the color to grab.

The Sony WH-1000XM5 are still among the most popular noise canceling headphones around. Two processors control eight microphones, and the noise canceling adjusts automatically to your surroundings, so engine rumble, traffic, and office chatter fade away. Four of those mics are dedicated to calls, which helps your voice come through clearly.

Battery life is rated at up to 30 hours with noise canceling on, and a quick three-minute charge gives you about three hours of listening. Multipoint lets you stay connected to your phone and laptop at the same time, and LDAC support delivers higher quality wireless audio from compatible Android phones.

They’re light for full-size headphones at around 250g, which makes long listening sessions more comfortable, and the soft ear cushions help with that too.

Sony has since launched the WH-1000XM6, but the newer model costs about twice as much. At $169.99, the Sony WH-1000XM5 deliver most of what people want from premium headphones for a much friendlier price.

items.body: Kodak licensee Reto this week introduced the SlideTag, a $34.99 Find My-compatible item tracker with a color E Ink screen for displaying personal photos. The SlideTag's design draws on Kodak's Kodachrome slide mounts, placing a square display inside a retro frame with an attachment point for a keyring. Its 1.54-inch screen has a resolution of 240 × 240 pixels and uses six ink colors to reproduce images. As it is an E Ink panel, it retains a static image without needing continuous power to display it. Users can manage photos through the Kodak Memory Link app for iOS and Android, separately from the accessory's tracking features. They can transfer up to 12 images over Bluetooth and arrange them into slideshows, or use the screen to display information such as contact details, a QR code, or a to-do list. Once paired with Apple's Find My app, the SlideTag can be located through the ‌Find My‌ network. There is also support for Google's Find Hub. A built-in buzzer provides an audible way to find nearby belongings. The device uses a replaceable CR2032 battery and has an IP54 rating for dust and splash resistance. Its plastic enclosure measures 39.3 × 46 × 7.58mm and weighs 16.6 grams, making it wider and taller than the current AirTag , but slightly thinner. Apple's tracker measures 31.9mm in diameter and 8mm thick, and weighs 11.8 grams. The ‌AirTag‌ retains some advantages, including Ultra Wideband technology for Precision Finding, which provides distance and directional guidance to nearby items on compatible devices. The ‌AirTag‌ also has a higher IP67 rating, providing protection against immersion in water up to one meter deep for up to 30 minutes. items.title: Apple Still Working on Giant Foldable iPad That Could Cost $5,000
items.summary: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "…
items.body: Apple is still developing a large foldable iPad despite ongoing technical challenges and uncertainty about whether it will ever launch, according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman . Speaking on the latest episode of the "Power On" podcast , Gurman revived discussion about the device, known internally as "Project J312." He described it as a foldable iPad with a display measuring around 19 to 20 inches, saying it would resemble a "gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside." The device could cost between $3,000 and $5,000. Apple apparently originally wanted to announce the device by 2027, before pushing that target to 2028. The timeframe has since slipped to around 2029, although Gurman cautioned that it remains uncertain whether the product will ever reach the market. Gurman cited cost and display manufacturing yield issues among the obstacles facing development, along with concerns that the ‌iPad‌ could be cumbersome. Apple has also yet to determine which operating system it would run, with macOS, iPadOS, and an entirely new platform all remaining possibilities. Gurman described the unresolved software direction as another complication, but expressed excitement about the device's potential. The comments follow a report from research firm Omdia in September, which claimed that Apple had canceled plans for a foldable MacBook measuring between 16.1 and 18 inches when unfolded. Earlier reports had described that device as a large-screened foldable ‌iPad‌, although it remains unclear whether Omdia was referring to the same project Gurman discussed. Gurman discussed the foldable ‌iPad‌ in April, describing it as a priority for John Ternus while warning that it could remain an unreleased experiment. The potential 2029 timeframe was already part of Gurman's report from October 2025 , when weight and display technology issues were said to threaten Apple's earlier 2028 target. iPhones Dominate China's Weak Singles' Day Smartphone Sales

Thursday November 26, 2026 4:55 am PST by Tim Hardwick

Apple held the top spot in China's smartphone market during the country's Singles' Day shopping festival, despite an 8% year-over-year sales decline, according to Counterpoint Research. The overall market fell 17% across the promotional period, defined as weeks 42–46.

Six of the top 10 bestsellers were iPhone 17 and 18 models, led by the iPhone 18 Pro Max, with the iPhone Duo at No. 9. Huawei was the only major brand to grow in the period, rising by 29%. Counterpoint says buyers are postponing upgrades rather than accepting higher prices, following strong iPhone 18 Pro sales in China at launch.

items.body: Apple could offer a limited-edition iPhone 20 Pro model that incorporates ceramic, according to the Chinese leaker known as Fixed Focus Digital. In a post on Weibo , the leaker claimed to have gotten their hands on ceramic components for the 20th-anniversary iPhone, which is expected to launch next year. The leaker said that production capacity for the components is planned to be very low, suggesting they will be for a limited-edition model. In a follow-up comment, the leaker claimed that the project would enter mass production if it passes engineering validation testing (EVT), and even joked that its scarcity could make it appreciate in value. The leaker doesn't say what kind of ceramic components they have in their possession, leaving it unclear whether Apple is considering a ceramic rear panel, a larger section of the enclosure, or a smaller exterior part. Apple already offers ceramic as a premium casing material on the Apple Watch Series 12, which comes in Pearl White and Night Blue ceramic alongside aluminum and titanium options. The company also previously sold ceramic Apple Watch Edition models, including a white ceramic version of the Series 5. Interestingly, the ‌iPhone Air‌ features Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back, and Fixed Focus Digital has previously said next year's iPhone 20 Pro models will use the same glass design , but with more pronounced curves along all four sides of a titanium frame. Ceramic Shield incorporates tiny ceramic crystals within a glass matrix, which preserves transparency while improving durability. However, the wording of the leaker's latest post suggests that ceramic could be applied in a more visually prominent way. quote.text: 三星、海力士、美光遭美国集体诉讼，被指借 HBM 转型操纵 DRAM 价格  诉状的核心论点在于：三星、SK海力士与美光凭借其在全球DRAM市场的寡头地位，在协同推进向HBM转型的同时，以这一战略调整为由大幅削减DDR3、DDR4等商用内存的产能，人为制造供给收缩。导致商用DRAM价格在过去四年间累计上涨约700%，对全球消费电子及商业IT采购造成广泛冲击。 ‎https://wallstreetcn.com/~

comments.text: 这一定都是阿共仔的阴谋.jpg

三家企业辩称，中国厂商正在扩大DDR4内存生产，给它们带来竞争压力，因此，逐步退出DDR4是正常的商业选择。

原告却认为，中国厂商当时所占的全球DRAM产能只有约5%，甚至更低，不足以解释三家企业几乎同时退出DDR4的决定。

更有意思的是，根据长鑫科技公开披露的材料，早在2024年底，长鑫就已经停止生产自有DDR4产品，开始向DDR5升级。而三星、SK海力士和美光，直到2025年4月至6月才相继宣布逐步退出主流DDR4生产。‎
